title: Stock Material error message markup and error-state policy bridge
summary: Source-level ownership of the stock Material validation-message child and its showError integration, with custom-control and rendering limits.

facts.claim: In Formly 6.3.12, the stock Material form-field wrapper places a mat-error element inside its mat-form-field after the field component insertion point; that mat-error contains formly-validation-message bound to the same field. The stock wrapper therefore supplies the validation-message markup for the Material form-field's error area; a compatible field using that wrapper does not need to duplicate that error-message child.
facts.context: Material form-field wrapper mat-error formly-validation-message beneath input error area custom field own error markup
limits: Describes the stock Formly Material wrapper template, not browser/layout/accessibility qualification or another adapter.

Using the wrapper does not by itself establish arbitrary custom widget, CVA or MatFormFieldControl compatibility; do not duplicate the message child solely because it is absent from the field component template.

facts.claim: Formly 6.3.12 Material FieldType connects Material error state to Formly's showError policy. Its errorStateMatcher.isErrorState returns this.field && this.showError. Its errorState getter calls this.options.showError(this), updates the cached error state and emits stateChanges when that value changes, then returns the policy result. Material error state is therefore not a promise to display an error solely because a control is invalid.
facts.context: Material FieldType errorStateMatcher errorState showError touched submitted invalid validation.show error display
limits: Applies to the Material FieldType bridge in the inspected release, not arbitrary plain core/custom types.
The default visibility predicate is separate and can be overridden; invalidity alone is not an unconditional display rule.
This does not implement async validation, pending-submit protection, remote-request debounce or immediate-correction policy.
